interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines suggest that a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger a biopsy. The guideline states, "a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy [135, 226, 264, 375], at the cost of missing a small number of mainly ISUP GG 2 cancers, especially in biopsy-naive patients or in highly selected populations with high prevalence of csPCa (in which the MRI NPV decreases) [372, 472]."

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
Expert-Structured's suggestion of biopsy is based on numerous panel variables, but the guideline makes the PI-RADS score decisive for the initial decision. Expert-Cohort's criterion confirms that the decision hinges on the PI-RADS score, not merely the presence of a suspicious DRE or prior biopsy status.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: at None the guideline does not dictate the next step, but the cohort criterion confirms that the PI-RADS score is the decisive factor.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
psa_trend - the PSA trend: the guideline does not provide a specific threshold for the PSA trend in this context, but the cohort criterion confirms the PI-RADS score is the decisive factor.
laboratory_results - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: unchanged does not support re-sampling, new or larger does
family-history anamnesis - the family-history anamnesis: the guideline suggests that in patients with low clinical suspicion of PCa (PSA density < 0.20 ng/mL/cc and no family history), biopsy can be omitted.

interventions.speaker: REGISTRAR
interventions.who: the registrar who pulls up documents; reports what they say, nothing else
interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
radiology_report
The mpMRI prose indicates that the lesion is compared against an earlier study by stating "Indication: Rising serum PSA (4.3 ng/mL) prompting malignancy evaluation," which implies comparison to prior status, but the specific comparison status (new/larger/unchanged) is not explicitly stated in the comparison section.
psa_trend
The PSA trend shows PSA rising from 1.2 (Aug 2023) to 4.3 (Jul 2024), with a value of 4.3 (Jan 2025), indicating a significant rise in the most recent interval.
previous_notes
The prior biopsy status is "None," and there is no existing surveillance protocol or planned treatment mentioned in the notes.

WHAT I DID NOT OPEN
I did not open the family-history anamnesis because the EAU guideline suggests biopsy can be omitted if there is no family history and low clinical suspicion.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
FOR sampling this patient now
PI-RADS score of 4, which is $\ge 3$, is a trigger according to the EAU guideline.
PSA trend shows a significant rise, suggesting progression that warrants investigation.
PRESERVES the decision because the PI-RADS score of 4 is the decisive factor according to the cohort criterion.

AGAINST sampling this patient now
The EAU guideline suggests biopsy can be omitted if there is no family history and low clinical suspicion.

WHERE THIS LEANS
LEAN: biopsy

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 4.30 ng/mL over 4 points spanning 17 months; velocity +2.70 ng/mL per year; doubling time about 7 months.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 6.7 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 1.9-23.4.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.81
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.69-0.93), of which 0.01 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents opened—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—address the core elements of the decision: the PI-RADS score (implied by the report context), the PSA trend, and the prior biopsy status ("None").

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the cohort criterion (PI-RADS $\ge 3$) was met, and the registrar confirmed no prior biopsy.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. Given the PI-RADS 4 and no prior biopsy, should we proceed with biopsy? This question is answered by the combination of the PI-RADS 4 (which triggered the cohort criterion) and the "None" prior biopsy status retrieved from previous_notes.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS score of 4 is the most critical variable because the EAU guideline and the cohort criterion explicitly state this is the decisive factor for triggering biopsy. The lack of prior biopsy is also highly weighted as it is a key feature in the expert models.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with biopsy based on the clear alignment between the PI-RADS 4 finding and the established cohort criterion, which is the primary rule governing this decision path.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
